label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
To: #general
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: none

@marco I’m pissed about Desert Palms. You told me Saturday all 14 units were done and the keys were with Yvette, but you didn’t put one bitting code in the sheet. Now Yvette needs three copies for 9B today and we’ve got nothing to cut from. On top of that, you left my black pinning tray with pins in it sitting on the counter in their leasing office.

This isn’t a small oversight. We did this same dance on the Kessler job in September, and I told you then to get the codes entered. Back in August I put it out to everybody in plain English: codes go in the sheet the same day, before you leave the van. Address, unit, code. No exceptions. That isn’t optional paperwork you get to when you feel like it. It’s part of the job, and leaving it undone puts the next man in a hole.

You’re going back to Desert Palms today. Decode 9B first so we can get those three keys cut for Yvette. Then decode the rest of the units if you can — I want all 14 done today if at all possible. Get every code entered in the sheet before you call it finished. Pick up my pinning tray from the leasing office and bring it back to the shop. Don’t leave it in the van and don’t make Lupe chase it down.

I’m not firing you, and I’m not saying you can’t do the work. You’re good with your hands. But being good with your hands doesn’t excuse ignoring the same instruction twice. I need to know you understand that.

Confirm here when you’re headed back out. Then update me when 9B is decoded, when the keys are handled, when my tray is recovered, and when the sheet is complete.
